claim: Jeffrey Epstein was found dead in his cell at the Metropolitan Correctional Center (MCC) in Manhattan on August 10, 2019, while held without bail on federal sex-trafficking charges. The New York City Office of the Chief Medical Examiner ruled the death a suicide by hanging, and the FBI found no evidence of a criminal act. The Department of Justice Office of the Inspector General (OIG) — the department's internal watchdog — documented a series of custody failures in its June 2023 report. The two guards assigned to Epstein's unit, Tova Noel and Michael Thomas, did not perform the required 30-minute rounds — prosecutors said they were asleep and browsing the internet during the roughly eight hours before his death — and then falsified the count and round records to show checks that were never made. Both were indicted in November 2019 on falsification and conspiracy counts and acknowledged the records were false; the charges were resolved in 2021 through deferred-prosecution agreements (100 hours of community service and cooperation with the OIG review). System deficiencies left nearly all of the cameras in and around the Special Housing Unit not recording from late July 2019 through the death, and usable footage of the cell area was not available. After a July 23, 2019 incident that placed Epstein on suicide watch, the MCC psychology department determined he needed a cellmate; on August 9 his cellmate was transferred out of the facility and staff did not assign a replacement, leaving him alone with access to extra bed linens. The OIG attributed the death to a 'combination of negligence, misconduct, and outright job performance failures' and said it found no evidence contradicting the FBI's no-criminality finding. The suicide ruling was contested by Dr. Michael Baden, a forensic pathologist hired by Epstein's brother who observed the autopsy: in October 2019 he said fractures to the hyoid bone and thyroid cartilage were more consistent with homicidal strangulation than suicidal hanging. Chief Medical Examiner Barbara Sampson rejected that assessment, saying she stood 'firmly behind' the determination of suicide. A separate documented detail concerns the removal of the body rather than the death itself: an FBI interview report (FD-302, case 90A-NY-3151227, interview dated August 12, 2019, released in the DOJ Epstein production) records that, with a large news-media presence outside the MCC, jail staff 'used boxes and sheets to create what appeared to be a human body, which was put into the white [Office of Chief Medical Examiner] vehicle which the press followed, allowing the black vehicle to depart unnoticed with EPSTEIN's body.' The 302 describes a decoy meant to misdirect the press about which vehicle carried the body; it does not indicate the body was anyone other than Epstein, and is distinct from — and not evidence for — the separate online claim that a body double was substituted or that Epstein survived.

notes: Fills a gap: the y2019 cluster referenced the death circumstances (false logs, dead cameras) in the narrative blurb and the opening poll but had no dedicated record. Documents the verified custody-failure facts and presents the cause-of-death conclusion as attributed both ways (NYC OCME suicide ruling + FBI no-criminality vs. Baden's homicide doubt) without adopting either, per the 'no official story as ground truth' rule. Surfaced via the Sammy Obeid standup capture DWHdAX2CF5_ — a comedy bit whose verifiable core is documented here: guards asleep & falsifying logs, cameras not recording, removed from suicide watch / cellmate gone, AND the body-removal decoy. On a re-check prompted by the operator, the comedian's 'boxes / decoy vehicle / real body in a black car' bit turned out to be real and in our own corpus — the FBI FD-302 at Bates EFTA00091322 — so it was moved from Group C to Group A; the editorial split was corrected 3/1/4 → 4/1/3. The decoy 302 documents misdirection of the media about the removal route, NOT a body swap; the 'shipped to Israel' destination has no primary trace (still Group C). The 'Fortnite login from Tel Aviv' claim is false: none of Epstein's email addresses in the files are linked to any Fortnite account; the viral 'littlestjeff1' account was a recent rename by an unrelated player, debunked by Epic Games' Tim Sweeney and the @FortniteStatus account (Snopes, Feb 2026).
